top3.title: Dirty Old Power Tour | AJJ
top3.why: AJJ (Andrew Jackson Jihad) bring their Dirty Old Power tour to Philly's most storied punk venue, with Greet Death opening. Folk-punk with teeth and a political streak, all ages, at a church that's hosted hardcore and DIY shows for decades. Doors 7:30, show 8; $33.02.

top3.title: Palestine Cinema Days 2026: Foragers
top3.why: Palestine Cinema Days returns with "Foragers," a documentary feature screening at Vox Populi, the artist-run gallery and project space in Chinatown North. A film program with explicit political stakes rather than a passive watch -- exactly the kind of screening easy to miss outside a dedicated series like this.

top3.title: BIG NIGHT screening & TIMPANO tasting!
top3.venue: Pen & Pencil Club, 1522 Latimer St, Philadelphia, PA 19102, USA
top3.why: Thirty years of "Big Night," Stanley Tucci and Campbell Scott's beloved Jersey Shore food film, celebrated with a screening and three Philly chefs' own takes on the movie's showpiece timpano. A members' press club turning a cult food movie into an actual tasting is the kind of unrepeatable mashup worth building a Monday around.

top3.title: NASH THE SLASH RISES AGAIN!
top3.why: Nash the Slash -- the mummy-bandaged, gas-masked Canadian avant-garde violinist and glass-harmonica player -- built a cult following over four decades before his death in 2014; this is most likely a tribute night resurrecting his persona and catalog rather than the man himself, but PhilaMOCA is exactly the room built for that stunt. $12, two sets (7:00 and 7:30). In Callowhill just above Chinatown; the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop is the closest way in.
